identity_cost.detail: No card and no hold: the free model is ordered without payment, and prepayment is only described for paid orders ('Any customer has to prepay each new order in our secured customer panel'). The registration form was read today and its required fields are: 'Email Address *', 'PIN for Email Validation *', 'Customer Type' (Private or Corporate), 'Salutation *', 'First Name *', 'Last Name *', 'Country *', 'Date of Birth (DD.MM.YYYY) *' and 'Password *'. A company name and a VAT-ID are optional ('VAT-ID (only for EU-Companies) (optional)'). The country list has 252 entries including 'United States', 'China' and 'Taiwan, Province Of China', so a non-EU signup is offered. The postal address, city and phone are NOT on the registration form; they are completed afterwards in the customer panel, and third-party guides report that the order only becomes effective once they are filled in. No ID document is requested anywhere read. Nothing was signed up for.

reliability_note: no reliability event observed. The known failure mode is procedural and documented by the vendor: a missed monthly renewal takes the server down, and the renewal needs a reachable email address to receive the PIN.

notes: VERIFIED 2026-10-24. It is real and it is orderable: the product page is live, the contract table and the vendor's own forum confirm the free model, and a non-EU country is selectable at registration. (1) It is NOT permanent. The contract is one month with manual renewal, the vendor answers 'yes' to 'do I renew by hand every month', and 'server becomes down' if you forget. Calling it 'free forever' is wrong; it is free for as long as a human renews it monthly, and the renewal now needs an emailed PIN. (2) IPv4: the free model includes NONE - the row is a dash - and IPv4 is an optional paid add-on ('additional IPv4 | EUR per IP / mo | yes, optional up to 16'). The price is a dash here because the page renders it client-side from an endpoint that returned the same figure for every row id tried, so the answer could not be attributed to the IPv4 row and was discarded rather than recorded. (3) The registration form asks for a date of birth and a country but NOT a postal address or phone; those go into the customer panel afterwards, and third-party guides report the order stays ineffective until they are filled in. No ID document is requested. The German page carries the same table, so the terms are not an English-only rendering. Signup URL: https://www.euserv.com/en/register.php, then the order link on the product page.
